title: Post-print realized-volatility term-structure compression gates pre-print trend continuation on print-currency pairs

mechanism.paragraph: Slow actor: institutional allocators, corporate hedgers and overlay managers who de-gear currency exposure ahead of a known, dated CPI uncertainty and re-engage only on their next observation/decision cycle (observation and transaction frictions, not price speed). Scheduled CPI prints resolve a dated uncertainty: the announcement literature shows realized volatility spikes into the release and decays quickly afterwards, while sticky-information agents update beliefs only sporadically. The proposed exploitable residue is in the LEVEL of daily realized volatility, not any session shape: when the short-window realized volatility measured across the print availability boundary is compressed relative to the pre-print baseline, the uncertainty-dampening phase has ended and slow re-engagement dominates the following week, so the pre-print trend continues with less noise; outside that state the same trend carries no edge. The mechanism consumes ZERO print content - only evidenced availability dates and price-derived volatility levels.
mechanism.forced_or_slow_actor: Institutional allocators / corporate hedgers / CTA and overlay risk managers with observation-cost-driven infrequent adjustment (slow actors); no fast-market actor is claimed.
mechanism.why_it_should_exist: Known-date uncertainty resolution plus sticky-information re-engagement produces a state-dependent trend-quality regime: post-print compression days are the window in which slow re-risking resumes an existing trend that de-gearing had dampened into the print.
literature_lineage: Mankiw, N.G. and Reis, R. (2002), 'Sticky Information versus Sticky Prices', Journal of Monetary Economics - agents update infrequently, so information diffuses slowly.

Alvarez, F., Guiso, L. and Lippi, F. (2012), 'Durable Consumption and Asset Management with Transaction and Observation Costs', Review of Economic Studies - observation frictions create delayed portfolio re-engagement.

Andersen, T., Bollerslev, T., Diebold, F. and Vega, C. (2003), 'Micro Effects of Public Announcements: High-Frequency Evidence from the Dollar Exchange Rate', Journal of International Economics - announcement volatility jumps and decays rapidly after macro prints in FX.

Jones, C., Lamont, O. and Lumsdaine, R. (1998), 'Macroeconomic News and Bond Market Volatility' - announcement-day volatility elevation without persistent post-announcement elevation (uncertainty resolution).
mechanism.novelty_statement: The information source is (a) evidenced per-print AVAILABILITY DATES (no print values, no print direction, no consensus) and (b) the daily realized-volatility term structure (short-window vs long-window level shift) from staged prices. It is not release-window position-avoidance (this family OPENS directional positions after availability; V5's family went flat into windows), not policy-rate carry (no rates input), not a session shape (daily clock only), not commodity-bloc risk-off conditioning. Wave diversity: distinct from axis-1 print-direction drift by construction (zero print content); D2 must still measure |rho| <= 0.20 against the full forbidden inventory.

row_fields_not_used: reference_period (no print values exist anywhere in this proposal)

prices.file: inherited staged daily snapshots for the 4 print-currency pairs, byte-verified per research/control/forex_free_v6_run/p2_data_authority_v6.json (manifest sha256 fe2155c0ef51bcac32262ebaf1c7d98fc724727eca1dda8b6644012ad854c460, 156 files, V4/V5 byte-identity chain)
prices.granularity: daily decision closes only; the 4h snapshots are NOT used by this proposal
derived_quantities: daily log returns at the 16:00 America/New_York decision close

availability_semantics.rule: A clock conditions the mapped pair from its published conditionable date: GB/AU/NZ DAY-precision rows are available for the daily decision on their decision_date by published construction (23:59:59Z end-of-day bound / offset-qualified instant per clock_semantics in the clocks file); CA INSTANT rows are conditionable at their published available_for_daily_decision_date.
availability_semantics.ca_boundary_rows: The 3 CA boundary-shift rows (decision dates 2018-05-28, 2018-05-29, 2021-07-23) are conditionable ONLY at their published available_for_daily_decision_date (2018-05-29, 2018-05-30, 2021-07-26 respectively); the release-date decision instant is NOT conditionable for them.
availability_semantics.gaps_fail_closed: AU pre-Sep-2019 quarterly rows and AU mid-2022 rows recorded as gaps in the clocks file carry NO evidenced availability and generate NO events - no interpolation, no synthetic prints.
availability_semantics.no_asserted_timestamps: Every conditioning date traces to a clocks-file row with its archive_sha256 (P-1); nothing else in this proposal is calendar-aware.

universe.mapping: each clock conditions exactly the pair containing its currency: GB->GBPUSD, CA->USDCAD, AU->AUDUSD, NZ->NZDUSD

excluded.evidence: no funded per-print clocks exist for EUR (p2_data_authority_v6.json: EMU status LEDGER_REPAIRED_NOT_A_FUNDED_CALENDAR), CH or JP (no calendar files in evidence), and US is OUT (p0c_unlock_verdict per p2_data_authority_v6.json); no clock maps to these pairs, so including them would require unevidenced conditioning (P-1 fail-closed)

clock.decision_instant: daily 16:00 America/New_York, DST-correct (20:00Z EDT / 21:00Z EST), per clocks-file clock_semantics
clock.decision_day_convention: weekday rule, FX 24/5; no holiday calendar is in evidence and none is assumed (next_trading_day_rule in the clocks file)

features_and_lags.notation: decision day t; C_t = decision close of t; r_t = ln(C_t / C_{t-1})
features_and_lags.rv5_A: sample standard deviation of {r_{A-4}, ..., r_A} (5 returns) at the decision close of the clock's conditionable date A
features_and_lags.rv20_A: sample standard deviation of {r_{A-24}, ..., r_{A-5}} (20 returns immediately preceding the rv5 window)
features_and_lags.trend10_A: sum of {r_{A-9}, ..., r_A} (10 returns ending at A)
features_and_lags.dead_zone: 0.9 < rv5_A / rv20_A < 1.1 produces no event (preregistered dead zone against knife-edge classification)
features_and_lags.direction: sign(trend10_A); no event if trend10_A == 0 exactly
features_and_lags.pit: all inputs are closes at or before the decision instant of A; the print day's close enters rv5/trend10 only when the clock is already conditionable at A per availability_semantics
features_and_lags.fitted_parameters: NONE - 0.9 / 1.1 / window lengths 5 and 20 / trend length 10 are preregistered constants; no training, no calibration, no threshold search anywhere

entry_exit_fills.entry_decision: at the decision close of A when state_compression holds (anchor) or state_expansion holds (neighbour); direction = sign(trend10_A)
entry_exit_fills.entry_fill: at the decision close of the FIRST decision day after the entry decision (next decision close); no same-bar fills
entry_exit_fills.exit_decision: at the decision close exactly 5 decision days after the entry fill
entry_exit_fills.exit_fill: at the decision close exactly 5 decision days after the entry fill (the exit decision close is 4 decision days after entry fill; the position is closed at the NEXT decision close)
entry_exit_fills.holding_profile: exposure spans exactly 5 decision-day close-to-close intervals; 6 bps round trip at stress tier 2.0 against typical 5-day FX trend ranges
entry_exit_fills.overlap_rule: one position per pair; a new clock signal on a pair with an open position is SKIPPED (no stacking, no pyramiding, no early exit)
entry_exit_fills.fold_boundary_rule: any trade whose exit fill crosses a fold boundary is DROPPED from both books and counted

costs.frozen: 1.5 bps per side x {1.0, 1.5, 2.0} applied at every fill (entry and exit each one side)
costs.primary: stress tier 2.0 is the PRIMARY gate; tiers 1.0/1.5 reported for the cost ladder
costs.dual_books: book A = net of costs at the tier multiplier; book B = gross price-only (zero cost); the gross book must not invert the aggregate sign of the net book (house dual-book invariant)

anchor.definition: post-print vol-compression state (rv5_A <= 0.9 * rv20_A) gates pre-print trend continuation: enter sign(trend10_A) at A, per entry_exit_fills
anchor.identifying_claim: the compression state is the load-bearing information

neighbour.differs_from_anchor_by_exactly_one_axis: state side: vol-EXPANSION (rv5_A >= 1.1 * rv20_A) instead of compression; all windows, direction rule, mapping, clock, costs, folds identical
neighbour.role: identifiability: the anchor must out-earn the neighbour on the identifying metric, else the vol term-structure axis is not load-bearing

control.definition: identical rule, identical state semantics, identical pair mapping, with every clock's conditionable date replaced by A_sham = next weekday >= conditionable date + 7 calendar days; must RUN under evidenced price semantics with non-vacuous decision counts
control.falsifier: if the sham reproduces the anchor (>= 0.5x the anchor's identifying metric, same sign), the effect is calendar-agnostic and the family is REJECTED

falsification_rule.identifying_metric: pooled per-trade NET return (bps per unit notional) on the stress tier 2.0 book, pooled over all anchor-eligible events within each held-out fold evaluation
kill_conditions: sham control identifying metric >= 0.5 x anchor identifying metric with the same sign -> REJECT family (calendar-agnostic earning)
neighbour identifying metric >= anchor identifying metric -> REJECT family as the named mechanism (vol state not load-bearing; it is plain trend)
anchor identifying metric <= 0 in ANY of the 3 held-out fold evaluations -> REJECT family (no fold rescue, no re-aggregation)
falsification_rule.no_rescue: no parameter, threshold, universe, hold, cost or gate change after any PnL is visible (preregistration); REJECT is a successful outcome

expected_failure_interpretation.anchor_fails_gates: no evidence that post-print volatility compression hosts exploitable trend continuation at daily frequency under frozen costs; recorded as a falsified shape, not a data problem
expected_failure_interpretation.sham_reproduces_anchor: the earning is calendar-agnostic (any +7d pseudo-print calendar earns alike) - the same null V5's sham measured; family dies as a calendar-conditioned claim
expected_failure_interpretation.neighbour_earns_like_anchor: the rv5/rv20 level shift is not the identifying information; family dies as a vol-term-structure claim
expected_failure_interpretation.non_vacuity_failure: if evidenced availability cannot fund the decision floors, the arm is NOT_RUN fail-closed - never rescued by loosening semantics

fold_contract.folds: 3 contiguous temporal thirds of S0 by decision-day count; boundaries frozen by A1/A9 before any scored computation
fold_contract.drop_one: the IDENTICAL frozen rule (zero fitted parameters) is evaluated on each third as held-out; stability-only folds - the family passes only if the identifying metric is positive in each of the 3 held-out evaluations
fold_contract.no_empty_folds: if any arm has zero decisions in a held-out fold, that arm-fold is NOT_RUN and the family cannot pass (fail-closed)
fold_contract.boundary_trades: dropped and counted per boundary-crossing rule

gates.non_vacuity_floor: >= 15 decisions per arm per held-out fold (A9 measures actual funded counts BEFORE selection; below floor = NOT_RUN)
gates.primary_profitability: pooled per-trade net mean > 0 at stress tier 2.0 in each held-out fold; per-fold PF and margins reported
gates.control_gate: sham must RUN and must NOT reproduce the anchor (see falsification_rule)
gates.specificity_gate: anchor > neighbour on the identifying metric
gates.dual_book_invariant: gross book does not invert the aggregate net sign
gates.breakeven_bps: break-even bps per trade reported per arm vs the 6.0 bps tier-2.0 round trip (P-2 knife-edge discipline)
gates.margin_to_fail: every gate reports its margin to its failure threshold (P-2)
gates.usd_drift: mean net USD exposure across open positions reported per fold (report-only for this 4-pair family; the family's claim is state-gated trend, not a persistent USD bet)

each_decision_row_records: decision date and decision instant (16:00 America/New_York)
clock row provenance: economy, decision_date, available_time_utc, precision, archive_sha256 (P-1)
state inputs: rv5_A, rv20_A, ratio, trend10_A with their exact input windows
entry/exit decision and fill dates, fill prices, side
costs booked per side at the tier multiplier and book (net/gross)
per_decision_evidence_traceability.recompute_contract: any data-semantics change (P-3) recomputes ALL THREE arms including the sham - a control verdict does not survive a semantics change for free

ancestry_disclosure.v5_release_window_position_avoidance: opposite action (opens after availability; V5 went flat into windows) and different information source (rv term structure vs calendar window); rho to be measured at D2
ancestry_disclosure.axis1_print_direction_drift: zero print content - no print values or directions exist anywhere in this proposal; rho to be measured at D2
ancestry_disclosure.vol_gated_carry: no policy-rate input of any kind; the forbidden family's rho measured in V4 was 0.997-1.000 on rate differentials, absent here
ancestry_disclosure.session_structure_families: daily clock only; no session windows, opens, fades or range structures are computed
ancestry_disclosure.commodity_bloc_risk_off: no risk-off event conditioning; AUDUSD/NZDUSD enter only via their own evidenced CPI clocks and a price-derived vol state

a9_open_questions: Snapshot close convention: confirm the staged daily snapshot cut aligns to (or maps fail-closed to) the 16:00 America/New_York decision close; if the staged cut differs, the mapping must be defined from the staged manifest BEFORE D2. This proposal assumes nothing silently - if unmappable, the proposal is UNAVAILABLE_FAIL_CLOSED.
Decision counts: how many of the 246 clocks survive (a) CA boundary-row remapping, (b) AU gap fail-closed rows, (c) the 0.9-1.1 dead zone - floors require >= 15 per arm per held-out fold.
Weekday/roll convention: print dates falling on days with no staged decision close (weekday rule without a holiday calendar) - count them and confirm the skip rule is funded.
Fold-boundary trade drops: expected count per fold.
Overlap skips: fraction of signals skipped under the one-position-per-pair rule.
